:::{#def-linear-operator}
#### Linear operator

A **linear operator** on $\reals^p$
is a linear map (@def-linear-map) from $\reals^p$ to itself,
that is, a linear map $f : \reals^p \to \reals^p$
whose input and output have the same length.
Some authors use "operator" more loosely, for any linear map.

:::

{{< slidebreak >}}

:::{#exm-linear-operator}
#### A linear operator, and a linear map that is not one

The map $f(\vx) = (2 x_1,\ x_1 + x_2)$ from @exm-linear-map
sends $\reals^2$ to $\reals^2$, so it is a linear operator on $\reals^2$.
The linear map $g(\vx) = x_1 + x_2$ sends $\reals^2$ to $\reals$,
so it is linear but not an operator:
its outputs have length $1$, not $2$.

:::
